items: A small change on the title screen.

The floppy (ADF) is now Logica 2.1 with the serial/parallel console switched off: the error summary page, the keyboard at the title screen, the CPU and memory in the top right corner, the LOGICAL logo. Before, it was Logica 2.0 with the ADDRESS ERROR REPORT fix, and only the mouse worked at its title screen. Thanks to Vincent Price for the report (an A1200). Logica's own parallel, serial and CIA tests on the floppy run as in 2.0 (no console shares the ports).
The floppy shows "Loading Logica ..." while it loads.

Memory test errors now start with a summary page, in the style of ATK: it gives the error count, the first and last error address, a grid of the data bits with the failing ones marked X, and the memory blocks with errors. The per-chip report then opens on the first block with errors instead of block 1. Thanks to jbilander for the suggestion.
The Amiga's own keyboard works at the title screen ("Press on any Enabled Input Device to Continue"). In Logica 2.0 only the mouse worked there. Thanks to jbilander for the report.
The title logo reads LOGICAL.

Every screen after the boot shows the CPU and memory in its top right corner, on the Amiga's display and on the console, e.g. `68030 FPU CHIP 2M FAST 8M` (`512K`, `1.5M`, `FAST NONE`). A screen that already has text there keeps it (the memory ADDRESS ERROR REPORT's title).

The patcher also makes a floppy disk (ADF) of Logica: Logica 2.0 with the ADDRESS ERROR REPORT fix, loaded into RAM, for an Amiga without a Logica EPROM. Boot from it or double-click its icon in Workbench. It runs on any Amiga with 512K: with less than 1 MB it leaves out the AGA pictures (an A500 can't show them), and then the chip RAM it occupies can't be tested. It has no serial/parallel console. Tested in WinUAE so far. The disk is packed, so it loads in a little over half the time.

The console keeps the whole boot log: until the AMIGA TYPE menu every step stays on screen, one per line, instead of each step clearing the last (thanks to kavanoz for the idea). On a board that hangs during boot you see every step it got through.

A boot summary before the first menu, shown on the console: - **CPU:** 68000 to 68060, with the 68881/68882 or the 68040's FPU. On a 68060 it also reads the CPU's revision register (rev 1, 4, 5, 6), shows full or EC/LC, and says when the FPU is switched off. - **Memory:** the chip RAM, and the fast RAM found at boot (Ranger, 32-bit, CPU slot, AUTOCONFIG).

Fixed a Logica 2.0 bug in the memory ADDRESS ERROR REPORT. The test counted an error but showed every chip as OK. Now the report marks the failing chip (for example C.06, D04-D07) on the right block. Thanks to jbilander for the report (A500 with an 8 MB SF2000).

Terminal keys work on 68000 Amigas (A500, A500+, A600, A2000): the receiver now keeps up with a 7 MHz CPU. Tested on a real A500+ rev 8: menus, digits and arrows work; a key is sometimes lost, never wrong.

Cable change: wire the adapter's TX straight to pins 10 and 12, with no resistor. The 1 kΩ resistor the old wiring sheet asked for kept a 3.3 V adapter's signal from reaching a real A500+. If your cable has it, bridge it. The wiring sheet is updated.

Logica 2.1 never drives pin 12 (POUT) any more, so the direct wire is safe: the parallel port test shows CONSOLE for it, and the advanced CIA test no longer pulses it (those steps were for a scope and still print DONE).

New tab on the patcher, "Fit a ROM to an EPROM": drop one Amiga ROM image (256 or 512 KB, plain or byte-swapped: Logica 2.1, a Kickstart) and pick the model (A500/A600/A2000, or A1200/A4000) and chip (27C400, 27C800, 27C160 / MX29F1615). The image is repeated to fill the bigger chips. The ROM itself is unchanged.
Tested on real hardware: Logica 2.1 (the byte-swapped 16-bit file) on an MX29F1615 boots an A500+ rev 8.
The patcher also accepts one 512 KB Logica 2.0 file (an emulator or 16-bit image, plain or byte-swapped), as well as the hi and lo pair. The ROM itself is unchanged.
New download for emulators: `logica21-emulator.rom`, one 512 KB image that is not byte-swapped. The ROM itself is unchanged.
The power LED blinks while the ROM boots, and stays on once the menu is up.
In menus laid out in two columns (main, MEMORY, DISPLAY, SYSTEM INFOS), ← and → move between the columns.

Any key (space, a letter) from the terminal now continues a "Press on any Enabled Input Device" prompt, on the parallel cable and on the serial port, so a dead Amiga keyboard or mouse no longer gets you stuck.
New: this web patcher.
Experimental: console output on the ROM socket's address lines, for a receiver (a Raspberry Pi Pico) that needs neither CIA nor Paula.
"Serial goes Parallel" on the title screen is one row lower, evenly spaced.
Steadier key input on the parallel cable.
The console is mirrored to the serial port (Paula), for Amigas with a dead CIA.
The title, About pages and version string say THE DIAGNOSTIC 2.1 / VERSION 2.1.
The CIA and parallel port tests run with the console cable plugged in; Ctrl-C breaks a running test.
Every screen Logica draws is sent to the terminal (VT100/ANSI), and keys typed on the terminal drive the menus.
Fatal boot errors are printed on the console.
First version: a text console on the parallel port from the first instruction on, with a line per boot step. The step LEDs are gone.

advanced CIA test wait: bchg #1,$bfd000 -> l21_waitpout (whole routine)

hex editor: tst.w $7bc(a4); beq.b $F8EB9E -> nops ($7AE alone admits the console)
parallel test entry: movem.l d0-d7/a0-a6,-(a7); lea $F8E9D5,a0 -> l21_par (mute)
parallel test, Remote Terminal connected (never: $7BC = 0): bra.w $F94F96 -> $F94F92 (the target is inside the l21_par_end patch)
parallel test CIA-B lines: lea $bfd000,a5; moveq #$e,d1; moveq #3,d3 -> jsr l21_par_ciab (from POUT: BUSY untouched, CONSOLE; POUT an output)
parallel test: bset #0,$bfd000 (BUSY) -> jsr l21_par_ack (the hint)
parallel test: bclr #0,$bfd000 (BUSY low) removed (branch target: NOP start)
parallel test end: bsr.w $F99820; bsr.w $F8E1B0 -> jsr l21_par_end (port setup, console back, result)
CIA precision test entry: movem; clr.l $7dc(a4) -> l21_cia_prec (mute, timer A stopped)
CIA precision test result: jsr $F8E1B0 -> jsr l21_cia_done (console back)
CIA advanced test entry: movem; move.w $7b0(a4),-(a7) -> l21_cia_adv (mute, timer A stopped, POUT an output)
CIA advanced test result: jsr $F8E1B0 -> jsr l21_cia_done (console back)
drive test: bsr.w $F8A874; cmpa.l #0,a5 -> jsr l21_drv_sel (mute, timer A stopped, flag cleared around the selection)
serial test entry: movem.l d0-d7/a0-a6,-(a7); bsr.w $F99820 -> l21_ser (Paula mute)
serial test end: bsr.w $F8E0DA; bsr.w $F8E1B0 -> jsr l21_ser_end (release wait, SERPER back, Paula unmuted, result)
